title: Prefetch-buffered autoscaler with safe eviction and burst buffering
creator: Anika Shah
description: Design and implement a prefetched-buffer autoscaling mode for Dedicated pools that targets throughput guarantees while bounding noisy scaling behavior. The feature combines short-term burst buffering (prefetch slots), queue-length and per-GPU tokens/sec as primary signals, and a safety envelope that enforces min/max nodes, cooldown windows, and eviction policies to avoid cache and KV warmup churn. Goal: meet committed throughput in bursty traffic patterns without overshooting fleet size or causing request drops during scale events.
acceptance_criteria: New autoscaler mode available behind a feature flag: 'prefetch-buffered'
Sustained throughput target: platform meets 95% of tenant committed throughput (qps/tokens/sec) across 95% of 1-hour windows in synthetic burst tests
P95 latency delta from steady-state <= +20% during allowed bursts for 90% of requests
Scale oscillation guard: no >2 scale up/down cycles within any 5 minute window under synthetic noisy load
Safe eviction: cached KV prefix eviction occurs only after explicit cooldown + prioritization; no more than 5% increase in cold K/V misses vs baseline
Automated canary tests and end-to-end CI (integration test against dedicated-sim harness) pass
Operational metrics and dashboards added: prefetch_slots_in_use, predicted_scale_delta, last_safe_eviction_ts
implementation_plan: Design - finalize metric composition and weighting (queue-length, tokens_per_gpu, p50 generation time) [Design doc link below]
Prototype - implement scaling controller shim that accepts 'prefetch-buffered' policy and computes desired replicas
Integrate - hook into capacity manager and admission controller to reserve prefetch slots per tenant
Safety - implement eviction gating, min/max node enforcement, cooldown window and burst budget accounting
Validation - synthetic burst scenarios in staging: 10x burst, frequent microbursts, and mixed-tenancy interference
Rollout - canary on 5 tenants, monitor metrics for 48 hours, progressive rollout to tiered Dedicated pools
Postmortem hooks - add incident playbook and automated rollback when miss-rate or retry-rate spikes exceed threshold
decision_log: 2026-02-23: Chose hybrid approach (heuristic PI controller + lightweight prediction) instead of full ML forecasting to reduce training/data requirements and improve determinism during outages
2026-03-01: Prefetch slots will be billed to tenant reservations to avoid capacity bleed for multi-tenant pools; implementation uses existing reservation API
2026-03-05: Eviction policy: soft-evict marking (deprioritize for new batches) followed by hard-eviction only after 2x cooldown windows; avoids repeated KV warmups
2026-03-09: Cooling windows set to dynamic double backoff (base 45s) for repeated oscillation scenarios to prevent thrash
test_plan: Unit tests for controller math and budget accounting
Integration test in dedicated-sim that replays 50 real tenant traces including sudden bursts
Chaos test: simulate instance termination during scale-up to validate fallback to lower-cost model variants
Load test to validate throughput guarantees with varying prefix/KV warmup ratios
observability_requirements: Event stream entries for 'safe_eviction_started' and 'safe_eviction_completed' with tenant id
Dashboard: per-tenant throughput vs committed throughput, scale decisions timeline
Alert rules: sustained predicted_scale_delta > 2x for 10 minutes; eviction failure rate > 1%

risks: Prefetch slot reservations undervalued -> can cause capacity tail that reduces effective throughput for other tenants
Excessively aggressive eviction can increase cold-cache miss storm leading to degraded p95 latency
Incorrect cost accounting if prefetch slots are billed incorrectly
Edge-case: long-running sequences may bypass token/sec signal and require per-request aging logic
mitigations: Conservative defaults on rollout (small canary tenant set) and billing-aware reservations
Soft-eviction and multi-window cooldowns to avoid repeated warmup churn
Telemetry-driven guardrails and automatic rollback if miss-rate or customer impact exceed thresholds
Add per-request age signal to adjust priority for long-running sequences in a follow-up patch
